sentences: After adding a rare Cuban stamp to his coveted collection and admonishing his butler for winning money in a rigged dice game in a Caribbean city, the retired thief, a retired jewel thief and unofficial private detective known by a nickname, meets a gorgeous young woman when she shares their horse-drawn carriage to the airport, to catch the flying boat to the coastal city.
At the coastal city's airport, they are ambushed by two kidnappers, employees of the crime boss.
The retired thief swiftly outruns the criminals with the young woman.

Initially reserved, the young woman confides her troubles to the retired thief: one of her boyfriend's clients was killed some time ago after retaining her boyfriend to send a package stuffed with $100,000 in bank notes.
The retired thief is discovered by the inspector and his buffoonish assistant along with the coastal city's police captain.
The retired thief evades capture and sets out to expose the three villains on his own.
The detective also realizes that his prized stamp collection has been swiped by the crime boss.
He tracks them down and has them arrested.
After many chases, double-crosses and switches, the retired thief exonerates himself and the young woman's boyfriend.
In the city, two private investigators, the detective and the associate, meet a prospective client.
She claims to be looking for her missing sister, who ran off from their home in another city and came to the city with a hoodlum.
The associate agrees to help get her sister back.
However, later that night, the police inform the detective that the associate has been killed.
The detective tries calling his client at her hotel to discover she has checked out.
Back at his apartment, he is grilled by a police detective and the lieutenant, who tell him that the hoodlum was murdered the same evening.
The lieutenant suggests that the detective had the opportunity and motive to kill the hoodlum, who likely killed the associate.
Later that morning, the detective meets the client, now calling herself by a different name.
She confesses that her story was made up.
She persuades the detective to investigate the murders and also reveals that the hoodlum was her partner.
She suspects he took advantage of her and killed the associate but claims to have no idea who killed the hoodlum.
At his office, the detective meets a dapper man, who offers him $5,000 to find a "black figure of a bird".
When the detective is skeptical, the dapper man pulls a gun on him and says he will search the room for it.
The detective knocks the dapper man out and goes through his belongings.
When the dapper man regains consciousness, he once again points his gun at the detective and says he'll search the room, to the detective's amusement.
On his way to visit the client later that evening, the detective is followed by a young man but manages to evade him.
When he tells the client about the dapper man, her nervousness indicates she knows him.
He arranges a meeting between the two at his apartment, where the dapper man becomes agitated when the client reveals that the "heavy man" is in the city.
When the detective goes to the dapper man's hotel in the morning, he spots the young gunman, the young man who trailed him earlier.
The young gunman works for the ringleader, the "heavy man".

In his hotel suite, the ringleader relates the history of the bird statuette, then offers the detective his pick of either $25,000 for the statuette and another $25,000 after its sale, or a quarter of the proceeds from its sale.
The detective's drink is spiked, and he passes out.
The young gunman and the dapper man come in from another room and leave with the ringleader.
When the detective regains consciousness, the detective searches the suite and finds a newspaper with the arrival time of a freighter circled.
He goes to the dock, only to find the ship on fire.
Later, the ship's captain, who had been shot several times, staggers into the detective's office before dying.
The bundle he was clutching contains the bird statuette.
The client calls the office, gives an address, then screams before the line goes dead.
The detective stashes the package at the bus terminal, then goes to the address he was given, which turns out to be an empty lot.
He returns home to discover the client hiding in a doorway.
He takes her inside and finds the ringleader, the dapper man, and the young gunman waiting for him, guns drawn.

The ringleader gives the detective $10,000 for the bird statuette, but the detective tells them that part of his price is someone he can turn over to the police for the murders of the hoodlum and the ship's captain, suggesting the young gunman.
After some intense negotiation, the ringleader and the dapper man agree and the young gunman is knocked out and disarmed.
Just after dawn, the detective calls his secretary to bring him the bundle.
However, when the ringleader inspects the statuette, he finds it is a fake, a copy made by the man from whom they stole it.
The dapper man lashes out at the ringleader, and the young gunman escapes during the tumult.
Recovering his composure, the ringleader invites the dapper man to return with him to a distant city to continue their quest.
After they leave, the detective calls the police and tells them where to pick up the pair, as well as the young gunman, who killed the hoodlum and the ship's captain.
The detective then angrily confronts the client, telling her he knows she killed the associate to implicate the hoodlum, her unwanted accomplice.
She confesses, but begs the detective not to turn her over to the police.
Returning to the city from the continent, the former thief tries unsuccessfully to strike up a conversation with attractive fellow ocean liner passenger the young woman.
He later rescues her when she is accosted by a man.
However, when he tries to follow her, he runs into his friendly nemesis, the police inspector, who wants to take him in on suspicion of stealing some pearls.
Knowing that the former thief's word is good (and that handcuffs are useless against him), the police inspector merely confiscates his landing card.
However, when the former thief discovers the body of the man who had bothered the young woman deposited in his suite, he has to break his word and debark to clear his name.
He trails the young woman to the seaside amusement park.
She has been followed by two men and is struck by a poisoned dart.
Before dying, she tells him enough to send him to the sideshow man, a midway performer whose act is pretending to be a robot or automaton.
Soon after, the two killers show up to report to their boss, the sideshow man, forcing the former thief to flee once again.
He hijacks the car belonging to the woman driver and manages to lose his pursuers after a high-speed chase.
The woman driver decides to help the former thief, despite his attempts to keep her out of his troubles.
They learn from a radio news broadcast that the young woman was a spy.
The former thief eventually discovers that an espionage ring led by the sideshow man is trying to take a stolen navy bombsight out of the country.
The police inspector and his men follow the former thief to the midway to arrest him and prove handy in apprehending the spies.
As a reward, the police inspector decides to forget about the evidence linking the former thief to the theft of the pearls.
The relatives of the old lady, an old unmarried lady living in the city who is reputedly good for three million dollars, try to make a judge declare her unable to take care of herself financially.
The attempt fails, and in charge of handing in the petition is the old lady's nephew the first nephew, a lawyer.

Instead he summons a newspaper reporter, the reporter (the actor), and his girlfriend, the reporter's girlfriend (the actress), and tells them he has been invited to stay a week at the old lady's estate up in the mountains.
The invitation states that any relative not arriving at the specified time will be excluded from the will.
The first nephew believes his aunt is mentally unsound and plans to kill them all during the stay.
Despite this, the first nephew and his wife, his brothers the second nephew and the third nephew, and their mother the nephews' mother keep the appointment.
As they arrive the old lady tells them that they are there so that she can learn which one of them should inherit the bulk of her fortune.
She also tells them that she keeps all of her money at the house.
That night the first nephew is stabbed to death in the library.
The reporter and the reporter's girlfriend receive the news of his death and show up at the estate with a photographer to write about the killing.

The sheriff is already questioning everyone at the house about their whereabouts during the night, and the reporter, the reporter's girlfriend and the photographer are all invited to stay at the estate by the old lady.
The next night, the third nephew is killed in the library, and the sheriff continues his investigation.
The dead bodies disappear and turn up again in the reporter's closet, but they disappear before he is able to show them to the others.

Later, the photographer sees the bookshelf in the library open revealing a secret doorway and as the old lady comes out from one side, he walks in via the reverse side of the bookshelf, unseen by her, into a secret passage.

The old lady asks the photographer to guard a small box with her valuables, offering him $10,000 to do so, and says she suspects her neighbor, the gentleman next door, of being involved in the killings.
The neighbor is supposedly in love with the old lady.
The second nephew is the next stabbed whilst he is talking to the maid, the old lady's house servant, in the garden.
However, the assailant is unknown as everyone present at the property appears to possess an alibi for the time of the attack.

The old lady is determined to catch the killer and tells the reporter of a plan she has, saying she will see to it that everyone is outside and then set the house on fire to see who tries to run in and save the money within from destruction.

When the house is in flames, the maid suddenly panics and angrily confronts her employer, stating that she should have the money for working for her for several years and tolerating her imperiousness, saying she was entitled to inherit something, and hysterically admits committing the murders, implicating also her accomplice, the driver, the chauffeur, whom she has secretly married.
She is arrested, and after a chase through the woods the chauffeur is also apprehended by the reporter armed with a revolver.

The gentleman next door then proposes to the old lady; the photographer presents the box to the old lady and gets his money, but the twist in the tale is that it turns out to be old defunct breakaway government dollars, and quite worthless.
The old lady then reveals that all of her 'fortune' is in the same currency, but the gentleman next door announces that it is unimportant as he has enough for them both to live upon.
The film ends with the reporter also getting the girl in the form of the reporter's girlfriend.
Married only a few hours, small-town girl the bride makes her first visit to the city with new husband the reporter, a hotshot reporter for the newspaper.
A body falls from a building.
The reporter steals the identification and calls in the story to the city editor, who makes the reporter follow it up.
Reporters' wives warn the bride to expect this kind of thing.
A personal ad leads the reporter to a second corpse.
The police read about in the newspaper and angrily haul the reporter in for questioning.
The bride's irritation grows, as does that of reporters from other newspapers at the reporter's continued scoops.
Evildoers from an anti-American organization kidnap the reporter, and when he won't reveal how he gets his information, they grab the bride as well.
The racketeer runs a numbers racket but likes the reporter better than these foreigners, so he saves the newlyweds.
A grateful reporter gives this scoop to every paper except the newspaper.

In the city, the detective and the detective's wife are looking forward to a relaxing afternoon at a horse racetrack, but they learn from the detective's old friend, the lieutenant, that a jockey named the rider has been found shot dead in a shower stall after throwing a race the previous day.
That night, the major.

The major, the special deputy for the state legislature, and investigative reporter the young reporter visit the couple, seeking the detective's help with the case; he refuses but accepts the young reporter's tickets to the evening's wrestling match.

At the arena, reporter the rival reporter, a rival of the young reporter, forces the owner's girlfriend, the girlfriend of arena owner and suspected racketeer the arena owner, to give him her diamond bracelet to settle a $5,000 debt.

While the detective and the detective's wife watch the match, the rival reporter goes to the arena owner's office upstairs and demands $10,000 for keeping the arena owner's name "clean" in the newspapers.
After the rival reporter leaves, bookmaker the bookie angrily tells the arena owner and his partner the business partner that the rival reporter owes him $8,000.
In a restaurant, the young reporter meets with his fiancée the secretary, who has been assisting in his investigation by working undercover as the arena owner's secretary.
The young reporter takes the secretary's office key and searches the arena owner's office.
As the young reporter leaves with the arena owner's ledger, a gun-wielding rival reporter arrives, demanding the ledger.
In the ensuing struggle, the rival reporter knocks the young reporter out and takes the ledger.
An unseen assailant then shoots the rival reporter dead, just as a night watchman sees the bookie running down the stairs.
After the match, the lieutenant informs the detective and the detective's wife of the murder.
In the arena owner's office, the police question the young reporter.
The arena owner and the business partner both have alibis.
The detective's wife happens upon a laundry list, which the detective determines to be a coded record of the night's illegal bets.
Nevertheless, the lieutenant has the young reporter and the secretary arrested.
At the racetrack, the detective finds a gun in the shower drain.

The next day, the detective theorizes with the lieutenant that the rider had been contemplating suicide before changing his mind, but as he tried to hide the gun in the drain, it accidentally went off and killed him.
The detective tells the press that the rider and the rival reporter were killed by the same person and that the young reporter is innocent.
The detective then tells the lieutenant that he hopes his false report will push the rival reporter's murderer to frame someone for both deaths.

A ticket seller at the wrestling arena informs the detective that the business partner's alibi is fake and that he witnessed the owner's girlfriend and the rival reporter arguing the night of his murder.
The detective visits the owner's girlfriend, who reacts angrily to the detective's questions and orders him to leave.
The detective then investigates the rival reporter's apartment, where the dog helps him find the owner's girlfriend's diamond bracelet.
The owner's girlfriend enters the apartment and admits that she was having an affair with the rival reporter, and that she gave him the bracelet because he owed the bookie $8,000 in gambling debts.
That night, the detective and the detective's wife meet the young reporter and the secretary at a seafood restaurant.
The detective encounters the bookie and tells him that the watchman saw him the night of the rival reporter's murder.
Terrified and wearing a bulletproof vest, the bookie flees the restaurant.
The lieutenant arrives and tells the detective and the young reporter that the rival reporter had been blackmailing the owner's girlfriend, threatening to expose her criminal past to the arena owner.
The major takes the detective, the young reporter, and the lieutenant to the bookie's apartment, where they find him hanging, as well as the partially burned ledger.
The detective remarks that the rough lacerations on the bookie's neck rule out a suicide, and that his bulletproof vest had been removed.
The next day, the detective gathers all the suspects in the lieutenant's office.
The detective eventually declares the major to be the murderer.
Since the rival reporter knew of the major's partnership with the arena owner and the business partner, the major killed the rival reporter.
He then killed the bookie and tried to frame him for the deaths of the rider and the rival reporter.
According to the superintendent of the bookie's building, the bookie, fearing for his own life, had switched apartments three hours before he died.
The major claims he had not visited the bookie in a week, yet he led the detective, the young reporter, and the lieutenant to the correct apartment the previous night.
The major grabs the detective's gun, but the detective's wife jumps the major while others help restrain him.
The detective reveals he had earlier emptied his gun and gives the detective's wife a diamond bracelet.

To boost listener ratings, radio personality the radio host encourages sponsors, of his murder mystery radio show, to offer a reward to anyone who can locate safe cracker the famous burglar, who is reportedly retired.
The reward for the person who finds the legendary gentleman burglar is set to $10,000.
There's little tough guy the hoodlum, who becomes over zealous over the possibility of winning the reward.
The famous burglar is rumored to have thrown down his hat in a picturesque small town called the town in the midwestern state.
The radio host and co-worker the colleague lead the hunt, together with the hoodlum, and it takes them to the small and previously quiet town.
The search begins in the small town's local newspaper, where the radio host hopes to find some old files that can reveal the famous burglar's whereabouts.
The radio host meets the daughter of the newspaper editor, the editor's daughter, who takes him to see her father, the editor.
It turns out the editor isn't willing to help out in the search for the famous burglar.
But the editor's daughter has taken a romantic interest in the radio host, and offers to help out.
She takes the party to the editor's gardener, the gardener, who she has heard tell stories about the famous burglar in the past.
The lead is a dead end, as the gardener claims to know nothing about the famous burglar of use to the radio host.

But when the radio host and the hoodlum visits the editor's house, the hoodlum finds the gardener rummaging about in the editor's office, destroying old files, and there is a photo of the gardener when he was younger, where his hair color matches the color of the famous burglar's side kick back in the day.
The hoodlum turns out to be the son of an infamous mobster who was framed by the famous burglar, and kills the gardener to revenge his father.
When the radio host finds out about the killing, he suspects the famous burglar of being the murderer.

He goes about town to collect fingerprints of important persons, and stirs up the whole town, since they are all ex-convicts, having settled down in this peaceful place to live a quiet law-abiding life.

The fingerprints are stored in a safe at the sheriff's office, and the radio host plans to ambush the famous burglar and catch him red-handed when he tries to crack the safe open to get hold of the prints.
Just as planned, the radio host catches the editor, who turns out to be the famous burglar, as he breaks the safe.
In an effort to save the rest of the town from being caught, the editor wants to give the radio host his prints in exchange for all the others'.
The hoodlum enters the scene and tries to get his revenge on the editor/the famous burglar.
The hoodlum manages to kill himself, and the radio host realizes that the editor/the famous burglar wasn't the one who killed the gardener.
The radio host tells the police that the gardener was the famous burglar in disguise, thus saving the editor and his daughter from ruin.
Then the radio host decides to stay in the small town with the editor's daughter.

During the war, the secretary, working as secretary for the highly reputed British criminologist the criminologist in the capital, is lobbying for legislation ordering the immediate arrest of all foreign agents stationed in the country.
The secretary is engaged to the criminologist's daughter, the fiancée, and is visiting the criminologist's mansion.
He is about to leave the mansion to be with the fiancée, who works at an air raid shelter, when he happens upon a briefcase in the foyer.
He looks through the briefcase that belongs to the criminologist's assistant, the assistant, before heading out in the night.
He is knocked out by the first warden and thrown into the back of the warden's ambulance.
The assistant happens to see the secretary go through his briefcase, and when he goes upstairs, he sees someone opening the criminologist's safe.
Before the assistant can do anything, the man is off with the plans for the government's new secret weapon - the beam detector.
The man drops a cufflink with the letter "L" on it.
The criminologist calls the police headquarters in.

Two American inspectors, the first visiting inspector and the second visiting inspector, are visiting the police headquarters and are invited by the chief investigator on the case, the chief inspector.
The three men go to the criminologist's mansion and conclude that the "L" must mean that notorious jewel thief the gentleman thief, the "gentleman thief", is the culprit.
An air raid hits the capital, and during the ensuing commotion, the gentleman thief meets with his valet the manservant.
The building closest to them begins to topple, and the gentleman thief saves the second warden from being crushed.
During the rest of the raid, the gentleman thief and his valet hide out in the air raid shelter where the fiancée works.
The gentleman thief tries to hide the plans, but the chief inspector arrives and arrests him for espionage.
The chief inspector does not find the plans though, and the manservant manages to get them back after the gentleman thief is taken away.
During interrogation, the gentleman thief manages to grab a gun and take the criminologist hostage.
He escapes and happens to meets the first warden outside, who gives him a ride, although not oblivious of his crime.
The first warden offers the gentleman thief a deal.
He wants to buy the plans.
In charge of the ring is the spy chief.
When the gentleman thief is taken to the German hideout, he also discovers that the secretary is their prisoner.
The gentleman thief explains that he does not have the plans, but he can retrieve them in a few days.
The assistant appears and explains that he captured the secretary because he was too nosy.
He also explains that the Germans intend to transmit the plans to the enemy capital with a radio transmitter at the hideout.
The gentleman thief is then released with instructions to inform the first warden when he has the plans.
The newspapers report that the criminologist has died in the air raid.
When the chief inspector visits the criminologist's mansion, he discovers a secret document sanctioning the gentleman thief to work undercover for the intelligence service to catch a ring of spies.
Later, the gentleman thief also makes contact with the criminologist's mansion, thus leading the police away from the mansion and to his own apartment.
The gentleman thief then goes in search of the German hideout, but discovers that the fiancée is following.
The gentleman thief tricks her into phoning the chief inspector so that there will be police reinforcements in the district surrounding the spies' headquarters.
The fiancée alerts the police of their whereabouts, and they surround the hideout, believing they are close to catching the thief.
The gentleman thief escapes the ring of police by riding in the second warden's ambulance.
The gentleman thief then returns to where he believes the hideout is, under the café, and finds the fiancée there.
They are both apprehended by the German agents and taken to the spy chief.
It turns out the assistant's real name is a different name, and that he is a German agent.
The three police inspectors, who have tracked the gentleman thief, are also captured.
When the Germans start broadcasting the plans, the second warden arrives and pretends to hold a stick of dynamite in his hand.
The German agents throw down their guns, and the gentleman thief explains to the Germans that the plans were fake, bait to find the spy ring.
The gentleman thief then gives the real plans to the police.
In 1935, rising French diplomat the diplomat and his beautiful much younger bride the young wife are celebrating their third month of marriage.
They are interrupted by a note from the mysterious blackmailer demanding one million francs from the diplomat in payment of an old debt.
Never having met the blackmailer, the diplomat has him arrested for attempted extortion.
During the trial which follows, the blackmailer claims that he knew the diplomat in 1922 as a petty criminal named the crook.
The diplomat maintains that amnesia he sustained in a devastating train accident that same year prevents him from remembering anything from that time.
The diplomat's identity is affirmed by the psychologist who treated him following the wreck, the first psychologist, ever since a family friend.
The diplomat's strategy is foiled by a psychologist for the defense, the second psychologist, who tricks the first psychologist into conceding the unreliability of a diagnosis of amnesia.
He suggests the diplomat fabricated his to hide his real identity.
In fact, no one really knows, as two similar men had boarded the train but only one survived.
Was it the crook or the diplomat?
The singer, a glamorous night club chanteuse, is introduced on behalf of the defense.
Upon studying the diplomat closely she looks startled and identifies him as the crook, her former lover.
The situation is saved by a surprise witness, the witness, who produces documentation proving that he and the crook were roommates in an African hospital and that the crook died of illness.
The blackmailer is convicted.
Shortly after, the witness confronts the diplomat privately.
He contends that the diplomat really is the crook, and collaborated with the witness and the blackmailer in a decade-old robbery in which a courier was killed.
He saved the diplomat at the trial only because he wants the million francs for himself; unless paid he will recant his testimony.
The singer separately corroborates that the diplomat and the crook are the same man, and that she still has feelings for him.
Offended by the diplomat's hostile response, she shows him a locket containing a photo of the two of them together, adding that she will offer this important piece of evidence to the witness.
Not long afterwards, the singer.
The singer makes a surprise appearance at the diplomat's home, implicitly threatening the diplomat with exposure and planting suspicions in the mind of the young wife.
The diplomat conceals his worries as much as possible from his wife, but has begun to doubt his own identity.
Anxious to see the singer again and draw her out further, the diplomat clandestinely visits her at the nightclub where she works.
Still treating him as the crook, she accuses him of faking amnesia to justify the betrayal of his former friends, adding that his mother is living in penury in an adjacent neighborhood.
The diplomat goes to the address the singer gives him and meets the aged mother.
She claims that he is not her son, but her demeanor suggests otherwise.
Meanwhile the witness and the singer confer together.
The real crook is dead and they are perpetrating a fraud on the diplomat, including the employment of an actress to play the mother.
The diplomat, whose unhappy and furtive behavior has begun to worry the young wife, collects his passport and tries to leave the country alone.
The witness finds out what he is doing and blocks his attempt to escape, demanding his money.
The diplomat protests that he does not have access to such a large sum, then unwarily mentions the government funds stored in his office.
The witness says that he can take the million francs from the diplomat's safe and make it look like an outside robbery.
The pair sneak past the guards at the foreign ministry and open the safe.
The young wife has been following the diplomat and now tries to intercede, but their argument is interrupted by the arrival of the police.
The couple, the witness, and the singer are all brought to headquarters, where the diplomat confesses to the old robbery and says he and his two accomplices must be punished for murder.
The singer panics and admits that the diplomat is not really the crook.
The diplomat reveals that he steered the witness to the idea of the robbery, then told the police to set an ambush in the office.

His doubts about his identity were laid to rest when, looking at his passport photo, he realized that the picture in the locket was a fabrication - allegedly taken before his accident, it shows him with a hairstyle he only adopted to cover the scar on his head.
The actress who played the mother is also arrested.
With all four blackmailers behind bars, the diplomat is cleared and his marriage and ambassadorial career are saved.
Scientist the inventor has discovered how to manufacture cheap synthetic diamonds that are nearly identical to the real thing.
When the inventor disappears, the police inspector turns to the gentleman sleuth (aka the sleuth) for help.
The gentleman sleuth is about to fly off with his long-suffering fiancée the bride-to-be and turns down the police inspector.
Jewel thief the female crook is part of the gang who abducted the inventor for his formula.
She tries to recruit the sleuth and when he declines, he is taken at gunpoint.
He escapes, tracks the inventor to a hotel and breaks into his room where he finds the inventor's twin brother the twin dead.
The police arrive and assume that it is the inventor.
To find the inventor, the sleuth allows himself to be abducted again, this time with his sidekick, the assistant, following.
He is taken to a warehouse where the female crook's accomplice the gangster is holding the inventor.
The gangster and his henchman the first henchman go to meet the dealer, a buyer for the formula, leaving the female crook and henchman the second henchman with the inventor and the sleuth.
Having been alerted by the assistant, the police arrive and the sleuth slips away with the female crook.
She now believes the gangster plans to double-cross her and that the sleuth has thrown in with her.
The female crook and the sleuth interrupt the meeting between the gangster and the dealer.
The female crook shoots the gangster, the first henchman escapes, the sleuth phones the police but the dealer knocks out the sleuth.
The female crook and the dealer discover that the gangster doesn't have the formula so they go after the first henchman.
The police inspector arrives and arrests the sleuth for the murder of the gangster.
At headquarters, the detective brings in the female crook, the first henchman, the second henchman and the dealer, and the sleuth is exonerated.
The police inspector is about to remove his handcuffs but the bride-to-be wants them left on.
She leads him away and they finally catch their plane.
